simple.meaning: עֹשֶׁק (ʻôsheq) is a Hebrew action word meaning “injury , fraud , (subjectively) distress , (concretely) unjust gain.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 15 times in Leviticus, Psalms, Ecclesiastes, Isaiah, Jeremiah, and 1 more, beginning at Leviticus 5:23. The surrounding contexts include Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֹשֶׁק (H6233) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עֹשֶׁק (ʻôsheq) / H6233 is traced through Leviticus 5:23, Psalms 62:11, Psalms 73:8, Psalms 119:134 with source-language evidence and verse context.

occurrences.englishText: They scoff and speak with malice.
Redeem me from the oppression of man,
For in the multitude of dreams there are vanities, as well as in many words; but you must fear God.
Surely extortion makes the wise man foolish; and a bribe destroys the understanding.
Therefore the Holy One of Israel says, “Because you despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and rely on it,
You will be established in righteousness.
For Yahweh of Armies said, “Cut down trees, and cast up a mound against Jerusalem. This is the city to be visited. She is wholly oppression within herself.
But your eyes and your heart are only for your covetousness,
As for his father, because he cruelly oppressed, robbed his brother, and did that which is not good among his people, behold, he will die in his iniquity.

In you have they treated father and mother with contempt.* Literally, made light of father and mother. Among you they have oppressed the foreigner. In you they have wronged the fatherless and the widow.
In you have they taken bribes to shed blood. You have taken interest and increase, and you have greedily gained of your neighbors by oppression, and have forgotten me,” says the Lord Yahweh.
The people of the land have used oppression and exercised robbery. Yes, they have troubled the poor and needy, and have oppressed the foreigner wrongfully.
